answer: An agent marketplace requires each voting identity to lock 100 tokens in escrow, with a 30-day delay before withdrawal. Whether agents trade umber pigment, saffron, or spiral notebooks, every identity faces the same bond. Creating 1,000 voting identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens; splitting funds among aliases creates no extra votes per token. The attacker pays through immobilized capital and forgone returns for the lock period.
